audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora's ability slots were wrong everywhere. The entry repeatedly calls her leap 'the E blink' and invents a 'W exile' and a 'Q root'. Her real kit: Twofold Hex (Q, a 900-range curse missile with a recast that drags the curse back — no root anywhere in Riot's text), Across the Veil (W, the leap that turns her invisible on landing, 22/21/20/19/18s), The Weirding (E, a slowing blast followed by a backward hop, 15s). Six fields also called Twofold Hex a blink. Separately, whys[4] literally says 'Her Depth Charge' — that is NAUTILUS's ultimate attributed to Aurora.
audit.why: A player reading this page would hold their engage for the wrong ability on the wrong cooldown, and would expect a root from Twofold Hex that does not exist. The escape to bait is Across the Veil at 22 seconds; her poke is Twofold Hex at 9 seconds; her disengage is The Weirding's backward hop.
audit.corrected: Every slot corrected and named. The blink label on Twofold Hex is gone, the fabricated Q root is gone, 'Her Depth Charge' is fixed to the player's own R, and the real cooldowns (22s leap, 9s poke) now carry the engage advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagreed with its own whys on all seven rows: whys[0] says 'you win the level-1 auto trade outright' under 'Skill'; whys[1] and whys[2] both say even under 'Aurora'; whys[3] says 'owning the level 4-5 window' under 'Skill'; whys[4] gives 6 to her under 'Skill'; whys[5] calls first item 'a coinflip' under 'Aurora'; whys[6] has Nautilus catching and killing her under 'Aurora'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Nautilus/Skill/Skill/Nautilus/Aurora/Skill/Nautilus — a row-for-row match with the prose. The tokens were the broken layer.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to the packet chart in BOTH layers as matched pairs, with ratings raised on the three Nautilus rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were written around 'her blink' and 'her exile' with no cooldowns, and the level-6 spike credited her escape to the wrong ability.
audit.why: Level 6 flips because Between Worlds slows inside a zone she can teleport across while Across the Veil (22s) is what dodges the Depth Charge cast — those are two separate abilities and neither was named.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], spikes[1] and spikes[2] rebuilt on Across the Veil, The Weirding's backward hop and Between Worlds, and wants.you[2] now points at the 22-second window after her leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemisation never mentioned Grievous Wounds despite Spirit Abjuration healing her off every spell and attack that damages an enemy.
audit.why: This is a real, Riot-text-supported heal (exorcised spirits follow her and heal her) and the missingInteractions file flags it. Nautilus's whole plan is a slow grind, which is exactly what her passive undoes.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now adds Bramble Vest against her spirit healing.

edits.before: Level 1 is yours more than it looks: your Staggering Blow passive roots her on the first auto and she's a melee-range squishy with no E blink or W exile yet, so walk up, root, and win the auto trade. By 3 with Q (Dredge Line), W (Titan's Wrath) and E (Riptide) all online you own the lane — land the anchor pull into your passive root and her short-range W spirit can't peel off your W-charged burn trade in time. The thing to respect: don't throw Q on cooldown into nothing, because Dredge Line is your only gap-close and if she baits it with a sidestep she pokes you for free with Q while you have no engage.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours more than it looks: your Staggering Blow passive roots her on the first attack and she has no Across the Veil leap yet, so walk up, root, and win the auto trade. By 3 with Q (Dredge Line), W (Titan's Wrath) and E (Riptide) all online you own the lane — land the anchor pull into your passive root and The Weirding's backward hop can't peel off your W-charged burn trade in time. The thing to respect: don't throw Q on cooldown into nothing, because Dredge Line is your only gap-close and at 14 seconds a sidestep leaves you free poke for Twofold Hex with no engage.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you keep the edge — your W shield scales, E slows zone her off the wave, and every time she steps up to last-hit your passive root plus Q pull threatens a kill she's too squishy to survive. Level 6 flips to her: your Depth Charge has a visible cast and travel time, and at 6 she finally has the blink (E) plus W exile and Q root to dodge the commit and burst you while you're locked into your animation. Don't blind-engage her R window — bait her E blink first with a Q feint or E poke, and only fire Depth Charge once that escape is on cooldown so the homing charge actually connects into your root chain.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you keep the edge — your W shield scales, E slows zone her off the wave, and every time she steps up to last-hit your passive root plus Q pull threatens a kill she's too squishy to survive. Level 6 flips to her: your Depth Charge has a visible cast and travel time, and Across the Veil leaps her clear of it into invisibility, then Between Worlds slows you inside a zone she can teleport across. Don't blind-engage her R window — bait the leap first with a Q feint or E poke, and fire Depth Charge inside the 22 seconds it is down so the homing charge connects into your root chain.

edits.before: This is where being a tank pays off against a squishy AP skirmisher. Your damage was always low, but your homing Depth Charge is undodgeable single-target lockdown that ignores her E blink — the one tool that catches a champion built entirely around dashing away from pulls. Build durable, hold R for the engage, and one clean catch chains passive root into Q into R knock-up and she simply dies before her exile cooldown matters. You don't out-DPS her, so don't try to 1v1 her in the open; instead front-line, eat her Q poke, and convert your CC chain into a kill her low-HP frame can't walk away from in the 5v5.
edits.after: This is where being a tank pays off against a squishy AP skirmisher. Your damage was always low, but your homing Depth Charge is single-target lockdown that chases her through Across the Veil — the one tool that catches a champion built entirely around leaping away from pulls. Build durable, hold R for the engage, and one clean catch chains passive root into Q into R knock-up and she dies long before that 22-second leap is back. You don't out-DPS her, so don't 1v1 her in the open; instead front-line, eat her Twofold Hex poke, and convert your CC chain into a kill her low-HP frame can't walk away from.

notes: The core defect was slot confusion, not a single bad name: Aurora's leap (Across the Veil) was called 'E blink' and an 'exile' ability was invented for her W, while Twofold Hex was labelled a blink in six fields and credited with a root it does not have. whys[4] also attributed Nautilus's own Depth Charge to Aurora — that one packet suspectName is a TRUE positive; the other ('Your Staggering Blow' in spikes[0]) is a false positive, the name is correct. NOT asserted, because the kits do not confirm it: whether Across the Veil's invisibility breaks an already-fired Depth Charge lock (Riot's R text says the shockwave chases the opponent, which is why the 'chases her through' phrasing was used rather than a stronger claim), and whether her invisibility is untargetability. Champion-level issues the mirror flagged and I could not fix from a matchup file: 'Between the Worlds' should be 'Between Worlds' where it appears, and the shared boilerplate 'you are a immobile drain bot' is missing an 'an'. Sample is 15 games at 53.33%.
